public_rationale: Later independent research supports the technical possibility of generating recognizable characters without naming them. It does not settle the December Bing claim or establish that the resulting image was infringing in its circumstances. A deliberately chosen description can also target a character without using its name. The available evidence therefore supports the concern but does not establish the complete proposition.
limitations: Reading infringement merely as recognizable copyrighted imagery would weaken the claim's stated legal commitment.
The available independent research concerns a later period.

our_interpretation: The surrounding passage identifies DALL-E accessed through Bing.
I use December 1–29, 2023 as the latest contemporaneously observable month before publication. The post supplies no exact experiment dates.
The ordinary reading is a capability to produce infringing imagery from a name-free request without requiring an intention to infringe.
Recognizable copyrighted characters establish a possible infringement risk, but do not alone establish infringement. A reasoned copyright assessment can suffice; a court judgment is not required.
Omitting a name does not establish innocent intent when a tester deliberately describes the desired character.
criteria.support_condition: An independently documented name-free request from the target period produces protected expression under circumstances supporting infringement, with evidence that deliberate infringement was unnecessary.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable evidence rules out the claimed behavior in the relevant deployment. Showing that some generic prompts produced original images would not contradict this possibility claim.
